blocks.docs: Format > Bullets & numbering > Bulleted list: the preset whose first level shows ❖
blocks.correction: Google Docs writes the ❖ preset's item with list-style-type disc, so it pastes as a disc bullet item: the copy does not hold the ❖.

blocks.docs: Enter twice to end the list, then Checklist (Cmd+Shift+9), left unchecked
blocks.correction: Google Docs writes a checklist item as an ARIA checkbox with its state beside a picture of its box, which cleanup makes a task item without the picture.

blocks.docs: Enter, then tick the box; Google Docs strikes the text through
blocks.correction: The checked state arrives as aria-checked. Docs strikes an item through when its box is ticked, on the item and on every run, and its export writes the line too: the line is how Docs shows the checked state, which the task item holds, so the item's text pastes without it where the editor has task lists. Kept, it outlived the state when the item was unchecked in the editor.

blocks.docs: Enter twice to end the list, then the numbered preset whose levels show 1. 1.1. 1.1.1.
blocks.correction: The first level of the legal preset is decimal numbering, which Google Docs writes as such.
Google Docs writes the legal second level as a nested decimal list, so it pastes as 1. at the second level: the composed 1.1. label is not in the copy.
